questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks)
questions.question:
1.
  a. What are infectious diseases (1 Mark)
  b. Name two ways through which pathogens /germs spread from infected person to healthy person? (2 Marks)
  c. Give two examples of infectious disease (1 Mark)
  d. State the pathogen that causes typhoid. (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Diseases caused by pathogens (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa) that can be passed from one person or organism to another.
b. Any two: through the air (droplets from coughing/sneezing); contaminated food and water; direct contact (touching, sexual contact); vectors such as mosquitoes and flies; contaminated objects or blood.
c. Any two: tuberculosis, cholera, malaria, typhoid, measles, HIV/AIDS, influenza.
d. The bacterium Salmonella typhi.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks)
questions.question:
3. Make comparison in between the two types of photosynthesis. Use the terms C₃ and C₄ to complete the following table. (6 Marks)

   | Features                                                   | C3 or C4 |
   | a) Use enzyme rubisco to fix Co₂ (1.5 marks)               |          |
   | b) Calvin cycle takes place in bundle sheet cells (1.5 marks) |       |
   | c) Have chloroplasts with no thylakoids (1.5 Marks)        |          |
   | d) Needs optimum temperature of 15 – 25c⁰ (1.5 Marks)      |          |
questions.answer_guide:
a) C3 – rubisco fixes CO₂ directly (C4 plants first fix CO₂ with PEP carboxylase)
b) C4
c) C4 – bundle-sheath chloroplasts of C4 plants lack grana (stacked thylakoids)
d) C3 (C4 plants have a higher optimum, about 30–40 °C)

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks)
questions.question:
4.
  a. Explain the term immune response. (1 Mark)
  b. Immune response can be classified into two categories. Mention them (2 Marks)
  c. Name only the first line of body defense (1 Mark)
  d. Explain how interferons take part in body defense against diseases (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. The body's reaction to the presence of a foreign substance (antigen/pathogen) in order to destroy or neutralise it.
b. Innate (non-specific) immune response and adaptive/acquired (specific) immune response. [Also accept: humoral (antibody) and cell-mediated responses.]
c. Physical and chemical barriers – the skin and mucous membranes (with mucus, cilia, tears, stomach acid).
d. Interferons are proteins released by virus-infected cells; they signal neighbouring healthy cells to make antiviral proteins that stop the virus from multiplying, and they activate immune cells.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks)
questions.question:
5.
  a. What are the two main stages that cell cycle consists of? (2 Marks)
  b. Match the four phases of mitosis (prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase) with their appropriate events given below.
     A. __________ the centromere splits apart and the chromatids are pulled to opposite poles of the cell by spindle fibers (1 Mark)
     B. __________ the nuclear membrane and nucleolus disappear and the chromosomes condense (1 Mark)
     C. __________ final phase in which the chromosomes unwind and become less visible (1 Mark)
     D. __________ the spindle fibers attach to the centromere after being lined at the equator (1 Mark)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Interphase and the mitotic (M) phase (mitosis + cytokinesis).
b. A – Anaphase
   B – Prophase
   C – Telophase
   D – Metaphase

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks)
questions.question:
6.
  a. What is castration? (1 Mark)
  b. Give two reasons for making livestock breeding (2 Marks)
  c. Why dehorning is important? (1 Mark)
  d. State two methods of dehorning (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. The removal or destruction of the testes of a male animal so that it cannot reproduce.
b. Any two: to improve the quality of animals (higher milk, meat, wool yields); to produce animals resistant to diseases and harsh conditions; to increase the number of animals; to obtain faster-growing animals.
c. It prevents animals from injuring each other and their handlers, and makes them easier and safer to handle.
d. Any two: using caustic chemicals (caustic soda/potash stick) on horn buds; hot iron (disbudding iron); dehorning saw; elastic rubber rings; dehorning wire.

questions.question:
7. Put the following events in the correct order for pollination by giving number (1 - 4) (6 Marks)
  a. Bee gets dusted with pollen ________
  b. Anther splits open ________
  c. Bee visits a flowering plans ________
  d. Pollen is deposited on stigma ________ (1.5 marks each)
questions.answer_guide:
a – 3
b – 1
c – 2
d – 4
(Anther splits open → bee visits a flowering plant → bee gets dusted with pollen → pollen is deposited on the stigma.)

   | a) ________ | Keeping and movement with livestock in search of pasture and water (1 Mark) |
   | b) ________ | Involves rearing both crop and animals on the same farm (2 Marks) |
   | c) ________ | Land use system in which trees or shrubs are grown in association with agricultural crops (1 Mark) |
   | d) ________ | Is usually practiced in areas of low population density or where arable land is not limited (2 Marks) |
questions.answer_guide:
a) Nomadic pastoralism
b) Mixed farming
c) Agroforestry
d) Shifting cultivation
